messages.subject: PayForge fees - updated analysis and what a switch would take
messages.body:
Dear Marta, dear Dev,

Following up on my January analysis of the payment fees. February volume was again close to €310k processed, and PayForge's 2.9% plus €0.30 per transaction cost us just over €9,700 for the month. Ledgerly's formal quote remains 2.3% plus €0.25, which on the same volume saves approximately €1,860 per month. Since January that argument has only grown, and we are now two months into paying a premium of roughly €3,700 in total for staying put.

I asked Dev for a view on integration effort before recommending anything. Dev, could you summarise your estimate for the team here? I would gently suggest that at this run-rate every month of delay has a measurable cost, but I am aware of the engineering constraint ahead of v3 and would not want to force a false choice.

Kind regards,
Helen Oyelaran
Chief Financial Officer, Parcelwise B.V.

messages.subject: RE: PayForge fees - updated analysis and what a switch would take
messages.body:
Helen,

My take, with numbers:
- Integration itself is smaller than I feared in January. Ledgerly's API is decent and I had Jonas spike it for two days. Call it 2-3 engineer-weeks for the billing service, webhooks, and invoice generation.
- The tail is reconciliation: we need one full billing cycle running both providers in shadow mode, so realistically 4-6 weeks end to end.
- Their native multi-currency invoicing removes a whole module we would otherwise build ourselves, which is maybe another 2 weeks we do not have to spend.

Honest assessment: this no longer competes with v3 the way I thought it did in January, provided we start the shadow-mode cycle soon rather than mid-launch.

Cheers, Dev

messages.subject: RE: PayForge fees - updated analysis and what a switch would take
messages.body:
spiked it as dev said. their sandbox is actually usable, which is more than i can say for payforge's.

one thing nobody mentioned: refunds. payforge does them in-line, ledgerly batches them overnight. nobody will notice except aisha's team on the phone with an angry customer once or twice a month. fwiw.

also their webhook signing uses the same hmac scheme as everyone else, so no drama there.

messages.subject: RE: PayForge fees - updated analysis and what a switch would take
messages.body:
Dear Marta,

With Dev's revised estimate of 2-3 engineer-weeks plus a shadow cycle, and Jonas confirming the technical risk is manageable, I would gently suggest we now put this on the agenda for the next leadership meeting. The economics have not changed: approximately €1,860 per month saved on roughly €310k of processed volume, and that is before any value from local-currency invoicing, which I understand sales is hearing more and more about.

May I propose we discuss it under finance on Tuesday? I will bring the comparison sheet.

Kind regards,
Helen Oyelaran
Chief Financial Officer, Parcelwise B.V.
